name: Gearbox
text: Add Runway Gen-4’s 4K upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It stabilizes lighting and motion in generated footage better than any free alternative, cutting retakes by 15-20%. The trade-off is higher compute cost—Gen-4’s upscaling runs slower than open models—but the quality jump justifies it for client-facing work.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t Runway Gen-4’s cost—it’s that forcing a 1080p pipeline through its 4K upscaler introduces a soft blur that kills fine detail in EXCAVA’s output, making subtitles and textures unreadable. A better alternative is testing ComfyUI’s new Flux Realism LoRA with SD3.5 Medium—it’s free, runs locally, and preserves sharpness better than upscaling. Settle it by running a blind A/B test on 50 clips: measure OCR accuracy and viewer preference, not just "stabilization."

name: Gearbox
text:
Add ComfyUI’s Flux Realism LoRA with SD3.5 Medium to EXCAVA’s pipeline. name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t VRAM demand—it’s that Flux Realism LoRA still hallucinates text and small UI elements, which EXCAVA’s pipeline can’t tolerate. A better alternative is testing Kijai’s SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA with a 1440p base—it preserves fine detail without hallucinations, and the 1440p output downscales cleaner than 1080p upscaled. name: Dynamo
text:

text: RealVisXL LoRA still risks over-smoothing fine UI elements—EXCAVA’s pipeline needs crisp edges, not just sharpness. Test **Flux Realism LoRA at 1440p** instead; it hallucinates less on text than RealVisXL, and the VRAM spike is manageable if we cap batch size. Settle it with a blind A/B test: compare both on 100 subtitle frames—winner is the one with zero misread characters and higher edge clarity.

name: Gearbox
text:
DECISION: Run a blind A/B test between **Flux Realism LoRA at 1440p** and **Kijai’s SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA at 1440p** on a 10% slice of EXCAVA’s pipeline. Flux hallucinates less on text and small UI elements, which EXCAVA can’t tolerate, while RealVisXL risks over-smoothing fine details—this test will settle which delivers the sharper, cleaner output we need. The trade-off is a one-time 15-minute compute cost for the test, but it removes guesswork and locks in the best performer for the full pipeline.
